question: ap1
stimulus:
I will arise and go now, and go to Innisfree,
And a small cabin build there, of clay and wattles made;
Nine bean-rows will I have there, a hive for the honey-bee,
And live alone in the bee-loud glade.

And I shall have some peace there, for peace comes dropping slow,
Dropping from the veils of the morning to where the cricket sings;
There midnight's all a glimmer, and noon a purple glow,
And evening full of the linnet's wings.

I will arise and go now, for always night and day
I hear lake water lapping with low sounds by the shore;
While I stand on the roadway, or on the pavements grey,
I hear it in the deep heart's core.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: The "Pavements Grey" Washout–Recall Assay
ideas.description: Mirroring the poem's speaker who still hears the absent lake while standing on grey pavements, stimulate cells (serum, TGF-beta, MAPK activation, or drug), wash out, wait a defined interval, then re-challenge, while separately tracking endogenously tagged AP-1 proteins (FOS/FOSL1/JUN), AP-1-motif chromatin accessibility, and transcriptional output. The memory signature is a faster or larger second response measured at a time when AP-1 protein has already decayed to baseline, which distinguishes a persistent AP-1 occupancy model from a latent primed-chromatin model.

ideas.title: "Nine Bean-Rows": Clonal Heritability of AP-1 State
ideas.description: Because memory implies transmission to daughters, barcode cells (CellTag/Watermelon-style) and sort on a live AP-1 activity reporter, then use scRNA-seq plus time-lapse lineage tracing to measure how strongly AP-1 state and the primed response correlate between sister, cousin, and more distant relatives as a function of generations since division. This partitions observed variance into heritable memory versus cell-intrinsic noise and yields a quantitative memory half-life in cell divisions.

ideas.title: "Peace Comes Dropping Slow": Timed Degron and Optogenetic Windows
ideas.description: Use dTAG or auxin-inducible degrons on AP-1 subunits, or optogenetic AP-1 constructs, to remove or supply AP-1 activity selectively during the encoding phase, the storage interval, or the recall challenge. Comparing these three windows separates whether AP-1 writes the memory, is required to maintain it, or is only needed to read it out, which is the central mechanistic distinction the question asks about.

ideas.title: "Veils of the Morning": Single-Molecule Footprinting of the Stored Trace
ideas.description: Apply long-read single-molecule footprinting (nanopore methyltransferase footprinting, or CUT&RUN with long-read sequencing) at primed enhancers during the memory interval to ask whether AP-1 is literally still bound or has lifted its veil and handed the trace off to nucleosome positioning, DNA methylation, cohesin, or mitotic bookmarking. Including mitotic timepoints tests whether AP-1 bookmarks its target enhancers through chromosome condensation.

ideas.title: "Lake Water Lapping": Frequency Encoding of Input History
ideas.description: Deliver the upstream stimulus as pulse trains of systematically varied frequency, amplitude, and duration using microfluidics or optogenetics, then compute the mutual information between past input history and current AP-1-dependent chromatin and transcriptional state. This tests whether AP-1 behaves as a leaky integrator that stores a running record of stimulation history rather than an instantaneous reporter of present signaling.
